claims.label: Theorem 1 (Convergence of RGD)
claims.statement_original:
Assume the tensor rank of $\mathcal X^*$ is $\mathbf r^*$ and the input rank to Algorithm 1 is $\mathbf r\ge\mathbf r^*$. Suppose $\mathscr A$ satisfies $2\mathbf r$-TRIP, and the initialization $\mathcal X^0$ satisfies $\|\mathcal X^0-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}\le\frac{R_{2\mathbf r}}{(d+m)(1+R_{2\mathbf r+\mathbf r^*}-R_{2\mathbf r})}\lambda$, where $\lambda:=\min_{k=1,\ldots,d+m}\sigma_{r_k^*}(\mathcal M_k(\mathcal X^*))$ is the minimum of least singular values at each matricization of $\mathcal X^*$. In addition, we assume $R_{2\mathbf r}\le\frac1{8(\sqrt{d+m}+1)+1}$ and $\lambda\ge\frac{2(1+R_{2\mathbf r+\mathbf r^*}-R_{2\mathbf r})(\sqrt{d+m}+1)(d+m)}{R_{2\mathbf r}(1-R_{2\mathbf r})}\|(\mathscr A^*(\mathcal E))_{\max(2\mathbf r)}\|_{\mathrm F}$. Then for all $t\ge0$,
\[
\|\mathcal X^t-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}\le2^{-t}\|\mathcal X^0-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}+\frac{2(\sqrt{d+m}+1)}{1-R_{2\mathbf r}}\|(\mathscr A^*(\mathcal E))_{\max(2\mathbf r)}\|_{\mathrm F}.
\]
(9)
Recall $(\mathscr A^*(\mathcal E))_{\max(2\mathbf r)}$ denotes the best Tucker rank $2\mathbf r$ approximation of the tensor $\mathscr A^*(\mathcal E)$. Especially if $\mathcal E=0$, $\{\mathcal X^t\}$ converges linearly to $\mathcal X^*$:
\[
\|\mathcal X^t-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}\le2^{-t}\|\mathcal X^0-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F},\qquad\forall t\ge0.
\]

claims.label: Theorem 2 (Convergence of RGN)
claims.statement_original:
Assume the tensor rank of $\mathcal X^*$ is $\mathbf r^*$ and the input rank to Algorithm 1 is $\mathbf r\ge\mathbf r^*$. Suppose $\mathscr A$ satisfies $2\mathbf r$-TRIP and the initialization $\mathcal X^0$ satisfies $\|\mathcal X^0-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}\le\frac{1-R_{2\mathbf r}}{4(d+m)(\sqrt{d+m}+1)(1+R_{2\mathbf r+\mathbf r^*}-R_{2\mathbf r})}\lambda$. Then for all $t\ge0$,
\[
\|\mathcal X^t-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}\le2^{-2^t}\|\mathcal X^0-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}+\frac{2(\sqrt{d+m}+1)}{1-R_{2\mathbf r}}\|(\mathscr A^*(\mathcal E))_{\max(2\mathbf r)}\|_{\mathrm F}.
\]
Especially if $\mathcal E=0$, $\{\mathcal X^t\}$ converges quadratically to $\mathcal X^*$:
\[
\|\mathcal X^t-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}\le2^{-2^t}\|\mathcal X^0-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F},\qquad\forall t\ge0.
\]

claims.label: Theorem 3 (Upper Bound for Estimators with Small Loss and Global Minimizers)
claims.statement_original: Suppose $\mathscr A$ satisfies $2\mathbf r$-TRIP with TRIP constant $R_{2\mathbf r}$ (Definition 1). Let $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ be any estimator such that $\operatorname{Tucrank}(\widehat{\mathcal X})\le\mathbf r$ and $\|\mathcal Y-\mathscr A(\widehat{\mathcal X})\|_{\mathrm F}^2\le\|\mathcal Y-\mathscr A(\mathcal X^*)\|_{\mathrm F}^2$, i.e., the loss function value of $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ is no bigger than $\mathcal X^*$. Then $\|\widehat{\mathcal X}-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}\le\frac2{1-R_{2\mathbf r}}\|(\mathscr A^*(\mathcal E))_{\max(2\mathbf r)}\|_{\mathrm F}$.

claims.label: Theorem 4 (Error Bound Under Gaussian Ensemble and Minimax Risk Upper and Lower Bounds)
claims.statement_original:
Consider the tensor-on-tensor regression problem (1) under Gaussian ensemble design (Definition 2) and let $df=\sum_{i=1}^{d+m}r_i(p_i-r_i)+\prod_{i=1}^{d+m}r_i$.

• (Upper bound) When $n\ge C(\sum_{i=1}^d(p_i-r_i)r_i+\prod_{i=1}^d r_i)\log(d)$ for some large positive constant $C$, with probability at least $1-\exp(-c_1(d,m)\underline p)$, $\|(\mathscr A^*(\mathcal E))_{\max(2\mathbf r)}\|_{\mathrm F}\le c_2(d,m)\sigma\sqrt{df/n}$ for some $c_1(d,m),c_2(d,m)>0$, where $\underline p:=\min_j p_j$. Furthermore, for $\widehat{\mathcal X}$ in Theorem 3, we have $\mathbb E\|\widehat{\mathcal X}-\mathcal X\|_{\mathrm F}\le C_2(d,m)\sigma\sqrt{df/n}$.

• (Lower bound) Consider the parameter space of all $p_1\times\cdots\times p_{d+m}$-dimensional tensors of Tucker rank at most $\mathbf r=(r_1,\ldots,r_{d+m})$:
\[
\mathcal F_{\mathbf p,\mathbf r}:=\{\mathcal X\in\mathbb R^{p_1\times\cdots\times p_{d+m}},\operatorname{Tucrank}(\mathcal X)\le\mathbf r\}.
\]
Suppose $\min_k r_k\ge C'$ for some absolute constant $C'$. Then there exists a absolute constant $c>0$ that does not depend on $\mathbf r$ and $\mathbf p$ such that $\inf_{\widehat{\mathcal X}}\sup_{\mathcal X\in\mathcal F_{\mathbf p,\mathbf r}}\mathbb E\|\widehat{\mathcal X}-\mathcal X\|_{\mathrm F}\ge c\sigma\sqrt{df/n}$.

claims.label: Theorem 6 (Initialization and Overall Guarantees in Tensor-on-vector Regression)
claims.statement_original:
Consider the over-parameterized tensor-on-vector regression under Gaussian ensemble design. Denote $df=\sum_{i=1}^{m+1}(p_i-r_i)r_i+\prod_{i=1}^{m+1}r_i$. Suppose
\[
n\ge c(m)\left(\left((\prod_{i=1}^{m+1}p_i)^{1/2}+df\right)\sigma^2/\lambda^2+p_1\right)
\]
for some constant $c(m)$. Then with probability at least $1-\exp(-c\underline p)$ for some $c>0$,

• $\mathcal X^0$ returned from Algorithm 3 satisfies the initialization conditions in Theorems 1 and 2;

• moreover, consider RGD and RGN initialized with $\mathcal X^0$, then as long as $t_{\max}\ge\log\left(\frac{\lambda\sqrt{n/df}}{c_1(m)\sigma}\right)\vee0$ for RGD or $t_{\max}\ge\log\log\left(\frac{\lambda\sqrt{n/df}}{c_2(m)\sigma}\right)\vee0$ for RGN, we have the output of RGD or RGN satisfies
\[
\|\mathcal X^{t_{\max}}-\mathcal X^*\|_{\mathrm F}\le c_3(m)\sigma\sqrt{df/n}.
\]

evidence.location: Theorem 6 — complete original statement and every branch

claims.label: Theorem 7 (Initialization and Overall Guarantees in Over-parameterized Matrix Trace Regression)
claims.statement_original:
Consider the over-parameterized matrix trace regression under Gaussian ensemble design. Denote $df=(p_1+p_2-r)r$ and suppose $n\ge\frac{C(\sigma^2+\|\mathbf X^*\|_{\mathrm F}^2)}{\sigma_{r^*}^2(\mathbf X^*)}df$ for some $C>0$. Then with probability at least $1-\exp(-c\underline p)$,

• $\mathbf X^0=\mathcal P_r(\mathscr A^*(\mathbf y))$ satisfies the initialization conditions in Corollary 1;

• moreover, consider RGD and RGN initialized with $\mathbf X^0$, then as long as $t_{\max}\ge\log\left(\frac{\sigma_{r^*}(\mathbf X^*)}{c_1\sigma}\sqrt{n/df}\right)\vee0$ for RGD or $t_{\max}\ge\log\log\left(\frac{\sigma_{r^*}(\mathbf X^*)}{c_2\sigma}\sqrt{n/df}\right)\vee0$ for RGN, we have the output of RGD or RGN satisfies
\[
\|\mathbf X^{t_{\max}}-\mathbf X^*\|_{\mathrm F}\le c_3\sigma\sqrt{df/n}.
\]

claims.label: Theorem 9 (Low-degree Hardness for Scalar-on-tensor Regression)
claims.statement_original:
Consider the hypothesis test (14). For any $0<\delta<1$, if $n\le\frac{(p/dD)^{d/2}\delta}{2(1-\sigma^2)}$, we have
\[
\sup_{\substack{\deg(f)\le D\\\text{polynomial }f:\ \mathbb E_{H_0}f(\{y_i,\mathcal A_i\}_{i=1}^n)=0,\\\operatorname{Var}_{H_0}f(\{y_i,\mathcal A_i\}_{i=1}^n)=1}}\mathbb E_{H_1}f(\{y_i,\mathcal A_i\}_{i=1}^n)\le\frac\delta{1-\delta}.
\]
(15)

claims.label: Theorem 10 (Perturbation Bound for Over-parameterized Tensor Decomposition)
claims.statement_original:
Suppose $\widetilde{\mathcal T},\mathcal T\in\mathbb R^{p_1\times\cdots\times p_d}$, $\mathcal T$ is of Tucker rank $\mathbf r^*=(r_1^*,\ldots,r_d^*)$ with Tucker decomposition $\mathcal B\times_1\mathbf U_1\times\cdots\times_d\mathbf U_d$, where $\mathcal B\in\mathbb R^{r_1^*\times\cdots\times r_d^*}$ and $\mathbf U_k\in\mathbb O_{p_k,r_k^*}$ for $k=1,\ldots,d$.
Let $\mathcal Z=\widetilde{\mathcal T}-\mathcal T$. Suppose the inputs of the OHOOI algorithm are $\widetilde{\mathcal T}$, Tucker rank $\mathbf r=(r_1,\ldots,r_d)$ with $\mathbf r\ge\mathbf r^*$ and initializations $\widetilde{\mathbf U}_k^0\in\mathbb O_{p_k,r_k}$ for $k=1,\ldots,d$. If the initialization error satisfies $\max_{k=1,\ldots,d}\|\widetilde{\mathbf U}_{k\perp}^{0\top}\mathbf U_k\|\le\frac{\sqrt2}2$. Then the output of Algorithm 5, $\widehat{\mathcal T}$, satisfies
\[
\|\widehat{\mathcal T}-\mathcal T\|_{\mathrm F}\le(2^{(d+1)/2}\cdot d+1)\|\mathcal Z_{\max(\mathbf r)}\|_{\mathrm F}.
\]

evidence.location: Theorem 10 — complete original statement and every branch
